grand_strategy.reading:
Türkiye runs the grand strategy of a middle power that has decided to be a hinge
rather than a bloc member: it keeps the second-largest army in NATO and hosts its
2026 summit, buys Russian gas and an S-400, signs a mutual-defence pact with
Riyadh and Islamabad, and offers itself as the venue and mediator that every
side needs. The currency is indispensability, and it works because nobody can
afford to push Ankara out. Luttwak's pattern appears at each seam: the S-400 that
proved autonomy cost the F-35; the victory in Syria draws Israeli bombs on its
airbase; the Blue Homeland decrees imperil the customs union; the boycott of
Israel closes the Gaza seat. Underneath sits regime security. The two things the
leadership most needs in 2026 - the end of the PKK war (Law 7595, the SDF's
dissolution) and a path to keep power (the İmamoğlu trial) - are domestic
before they are foreign, and they set the tone of the external line: a
'Terror-Free Türkiye' that justifies Syrian and Iraqi policy, and a Western
reconciliation (Trump's promise of sanctions relief and the F-35) pursued
without conditions on rule of law. Signals that are not rows: Ankara has not
joined Western sanctions on Russia and cut Russian crude only after Trump's
appeal of Sept 2025; Washington's envoy to Syria is also its ambassador in
Ankara, which makes Turkey the channel for US policy in Damascus. The open
questions for the next quarter are whether Trump's promise becomes a legal
instrument, whether the Blue Homeland law passes in October, and whether the
Israel-Turkey deconfliction mechanism in Syria is built before the next strike.
